body:
Luxembourg’s private debt fund market recorded 23% growth in assets under management (AuM) in 2025, driven by investor demand and a shift towards direct lending strategies, according to a survey by KPMG Luxembourg together with the Association of the Luxembourg Fund Industry (Alfi).

Debt-originating funds accounted for 66% of surveyed funds, up from 50% a year earlier, while debt-participating funds declined from 48% to 26%.

EU member states accounted for 54% of geographical allocations, followed by other European countries at 19% and North America at 15%.

Reserved alternative investment funds continued to dominate Luxembourg’s private debt fund structures, representing 70% of relevant funds, up from 64% previously. Special limited partnerships accounted for 82% of legal forms among other alternative investment Funds, while closed ended structures represented 89% of the market.

Institutional investors remained the largest investor group, accounting for 79% of the total, with European investors comprising 73% of the investor base.

The survey also found that 48% of private debt funds targeted annual returns between 6% and 10%, compared with 57% previously.

Julien Bieber, partner tax, alternative investments at KPMG in Luxembourg, said: “ Luxembourg’s private debt market is expanding in both scale and ambition. The rise of direct lending shows managers taking a more active role in financing businesses and the wider economy. As the market matures, its continued success will depend not only on growth, but also on disciplined underwriting, sound valuations and investor confidence.”

Britta Borneff, chief marketing officer at ALFI, added: “The sustained growth of Luxembourg’s private debt market underscores the importance of this asset class as a source of financing for the real economy. However, growth will depend on maintaining sound underwriting standards, robust governance frameworks and high levels of transparency. Preserving investor confidence will be essential as the market continues to evolve and mature. By providing greater visibility into the Luxembourg private debt fund market, this survey provides valuable insights into its development, key trends and the challenges that lie ahead.”

The survey analysed data from 12 depositaries representing more than 1,900 funds and sub-funds investing in private debt.
